title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the continuation of the 'Longue Marche' Grothendieck studies a group extension G_{ρ,σ}. It is generated by elements ρ and σ with ρ'=ξρ and σ'=ησ. There is a central element ω, with μ_G={1,ω} and ω=1 after dividing by μ_G. This looks like the SL2(Z)/PSL2(Z)-type presentation tied to π1 of M_{1,1} and the projective line minus three points.

The extension G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G sits over Φ_12^* × G_3. Here G_3 is the symmetric group S_3 viewed as a constant group scheme. Φ_12^* is a group-like object whose points over Spec(Ẑ) give Ẑ^* (next page), so the Ẑ^*-part plays the role of the cyclotomic character. The kernel is an abelian group M, written additively. It has generators λ0, λ1 and δ=λ1-λ0, which behave like the abelianized inertia classes of P^1-{0,1,∞}.

For each μ in Ẑ^*, a standard lift u_μ was defined earlier, in (150, 151), with u_μ(η)=η^μ. A general candidate lift of μ is λ·u_μ with λ = xλ0 + yλ1 in M. A splitting of the S_3-part is parametrized by ρ'=ξρ and σ'=ησ, with ξ=a0λ0+a1λ1 and η=bδ. These are subject to the condition (263) coming from the defining relations.

Requiring that λu_μ commutes correctly with ρ' and σ' gives the linear system (262) in x and y. Its first and third equations give y = ν(-2a1+2b-1) and x = y + 2νb = ν(-2a1+4b-1), where ν=ν(μ) (probably (μ-1)/2, given the ω^{(μ-1)/2} twist on σ).

This page substitutes these into the second equation, x+y = -2νa0. This gives ν(-4a1+6b-2) = -2νa0, i.e. 2ν(a0-2a1+3b-1)=0. The system is therefore not overdetermined: this is automatically satisfied by the constraint (263) on (a0,a1,b).

Hence the Proposition. Every splitting H of the extension G^+/μ_G of S_3 by M (taken inside G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G, over an arbitrary base) extends canonically to a homomorphic section of the extension G^♮_{ρ,σ} of Φ_12^* by M. The section is μ ↦ λ(μ)u_μ, with λ given by the explicit formulas (264).

Corollary (266). The restriction map Scindages(G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G over Φ_12^*×G_3) → Scindages(G^+ over G_3) is an isomorphism of sheaves on (Sch)/S. Hence the source is an M-torsor, using the proposition on p. 702.

Over S=Spec(Ẑ) (next page): the splittings of G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G over Ẑ^*×S_3 by M̂ form an M̂-torsor, isomorphic by restriction to the torsor of splittings over S_3. In cohomological terms: every S_3-splitting extends uniquely to the cyclotomic Ẑ^* factor. This is a rigidity statement for the abelianized (metabelian) level of the Galois action on the tower relevant to M_{1,1} / P^1-{0,1,∞}.
errors: Previous-page transcription of (264) reads y=-ν(-2a1+2b-1). Solving the first and third equations of (262) actually gives y=ν(-2a1+2b-1). Only this sign makes x=y+2νb=ν(-2a1+4b-1) and x+y=ν(-4a1+6b-2) (as on this page) consistent. So it is a transcription or slip sign error, not a mathematical one.

This page derives the condition a0-2a1+3b-1=0 and calls it a consequence of (263). (263) as transcribed on the previous page is -2a0+2a1-3b+1=0, which is not proportional to it. Either the transcription of (263) is wrong (likely -a0+2a1-3b+1=0) or there is a slip on the earlier page; this cannot be settled from this page alone.

The factor 2ν: when 2 is not invertible (e.g. 2-torsion in M), '2ν(...)=0' follows from (263) but the reasoning implicitly treats this as a linear identity. That is fine as stated, since it is a consequence rather than a constraint, so no gap arises.

ideas.what: Unique extension of an S_3-splitting of an abelianized π1-extension to a splitting over Ẑ^* × S_3, with explicit cocycle λ(μ)=xλ0+yλ1 linear in ν(μ)
ideas.modern_name: Restriction isomorphism on splittings / H^1 computation for the cyclotomic Ẑ^*-action on abelianized π1 (metabelian level of Galois action on P^1-{0,1,∞} / M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in anabelian / Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature (Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura) at the abelian/metabelian level
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know; this is the unpublished continuation (pp. 650bis–787).

ideas.what: Formulating splittings as a sheaf on (Sch)/S that is a torsor under the group scheme M, then specializing to S=Spec(Ẑ)
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of sections of an extension of group schemes (sheaf-theoretic H^1)
ideas.where_published: General framework as in SGA 3; this specific application is unpublished.

missed.claim: An explicit, base-independent (scheme-theoretic) formula for the unique Ẑ^*-equivariant extension of S_3-splittings in the SL2/M_{1,1}-type extension G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G. It reduces to the observation that the overdetermined linear system has rank 2 thanks to the defining relation. Of documentary interest for how Grothendieck handled the 'Teichmüller tower in dimension 1' at the abelianized level; mathematically elementary.
missed.quote: 2ν(a0−2a1+3b−1)=0 qui est une conséquence de (263)! ... L'homomorphisme canonique ... Scindages(G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G sur Φ*_12×G_3) → Scindages(G^+ au-dessus de G_3)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it documents Grothendieck's explicit treatment of the cyclotomic part of the Galois action on the abelianized modular tower. Experts would regard the result as a routine cohomology computation.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine linear-algebra and group-cohomology verification inside a longer unpublished computation. The result (S_3-splittings extend uniquely along the cyclotomic Ẑ^* factor at the abelianized level) is expected and would not surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Pour H scindage de l'ext. G^+/μ_G de (G_3)_S' – the subscript after G_3 is likely the base S (crossed-out letter), not G.

Line reading 'le composé [?] que sa section est' is probably 'le commutant (dans le cas quelconque), ... est un homomorphisme section' – the image is ambiguous. The insertion appears to read '(scindage dans G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G, dans le cas quelconque)'.
'a0, a1, b ∈ Γ G_0' likely 'a0, a1, b ∈ Γ(G_a)' or 'Γ(O_S)', i.e. sections of the structure sheaf / additive group; similarly 'x, y ∈ Γ G_a'.
(265) should read u_{ρ',σ'}(μ) = λ u_μ (with μ underlined), as transcribed.
Previous page (264): y = ν(−2a1+2b−1), without the extra leading minus sign.
